title: India's Athletics Campaign Opens at CWG 2026 With Three High Jumpers Eyeing Medals
excerpt: National record holder Sarvesh Kushare leads a strong Indian contingent in the men's high jump final at Scotstoun Stadium as track and field events begin on Day 5 in Glasgow.
body:
• India fields three high jumpers — Sarvesh Kushare, Tejaswin Shankar, and J Aadarsh Ram — in the men's final at Scotstoun Stadium on Day 5 of CWG 2026.
  • Kushare holds the national record at 2.31m, matching England's Kimani Jack as the top-ranked Commonwealth jumper this season.
  • Shankar, the 2022 CWG bronze medalist, competes alongside Kushare in a rivalry that has elevated Indian high jumping to new heights.
  • India's medal tally stands at six after Day 4, with weightlifting delivering the bulk of podium finishes; athletics offers the next wave of medal opportunities.

High Jump Headlines India's Track and Field Debut

India's athletics campaign at the 2026 Commonwealth Games kicks off on Monday at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium, with the men's high jump final the marquee event of the day. Three Indians — Sarvesh Kushare, Tejaswin Shankar, and J Aadarsh Ram — will contest the straight final in what shapes up as India's strongest medal prospect on the track.

Kushare enters the competition as the favourite among Commonwealth athletes. The 31-year-old from Devgaon broke the Indian national record earlier this year with a leap of 2.31m, displacing Shankar at the top of the country's all-time list. That mark ties England's Kimani Jack as the best among Commonwealth nations this season, ahead of Jamaica's Romaine Beckford at 2.30m.

"I will go for gold at the Asian Games and I am confident about it. The 2.35m mark will also fall, maybe during the Commonwealth or the Asian Games."

— Sarvesh Kushare, Indian High Jumper

A Rivalry That Lifted Indian High Jumping

The Kushare-Shankar dynamic has redefined expectations for Indian high jumping. Before Shankar's emergence in 2015-16, no Indian athlete had cleared 2.20m. Shankar broke through that ceiling, won bronze at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games, and held the national record until Kushare surpassed it.

Kushare has acknowledged Shankar's role in raising the bar. "Before 2015-16, no Indian could go above 2.20m. Tejaswin did that, and after that we also felt that we can do it," Kushare told reporters after setting the national record. Shankar, who carries a season-best of 2.25m, will also compete in the decathlon later in the Games, adding versatility to his campaign.

Aadarsh Ram, with a season-best of 2.27m, rounds out the Indian trio and could factor into the medal conversation. India has never won a Commonwealth Games gold in high jump, making this a potential breakthrough moment.

Early Day 5 Results: Mixed Fortunes Across Disciplines

Before the evening athletics session, Indian athletes delivered a mixed bag of results across other sports. Weightlifter Gyaneshwari Yadav clinched silver in the women's 53kg event, lifting a total of 199kg — 88kg in the snatch and 111kg in the clean and jerk. Nigeria's Didih Onome Omolola took gold with a Commonwealth Games-record total of 206kg. Bindyarani Devi added bronze in the women's 58kg category, extending India's dominance on the weightlifting platform.

In the morning athletics session, Murali Sreeshankar and Lokesh Sathyanathan both qualified for the men's long jump final, while Tejas Shirse advanced through the men's 110m hurdles heats to book a spot in the evening final. Sprinter Gurindervir Singh, however, failed to qualify for the men's 100m final.

India's boxers had a strong day. Sachin Siwach won his men's 60kg Round of 16 bout 4-1, Ankush cruised through 5-0 in the men's 75-80kg category, and Sakshi Choudhary matched that scoreline in the women's 51kg draw, according to Sporting News.

Medal Tally and What's at Stake

India sits eighth on the overall medal table with six medals — one gold, three silvers, and two bronzes — all from weightlifting and para-powerlifting. Australia leads comfortably with 22 golds and 50 medals overall, followed by England with 26 medals.

The scaled-down format of these Games, held after the state of Victoria in Australia withdrew as host and Glasgow stepped in, has removed several of India's traditional stronghold sports. Shooting, wrestling, badminton, and table tennis — which collectively have accounted for over 300 of India's historical Commonwealth medals — are absent from the programme. Only 10 core sports are contested across seven venues.

That absence places outsized pressure on athletics, weightlifting, and boxing to drive India's medal count. The 126-member Indian contingent still harbours hopes of a strong showing, with javelin star Neeraj Chopra set to compete later in the Games.

What's Next for India on the Track

Beyond the high jump, India's athletics programme at CWG 2026 stretches through the remaining week. Sreeshankar's long jump final is scheduled for July 29, Neeraj Chopra's javelin throw final for July 31, and the mixed 4x400m relay on August 1. Para-athletics events also offer medal chances, with Sharmila Dhankar and Shilpa K Shyla competing in the women's shot put F57 final on Monday evening.

For Indian sports fans, the high jump final is the immediate focus — a straight final with no qualifying round, meaning Kushare, Shankar, and Aadarsh Ram get one shot at the podium against a field that includes Jamaica's Beckford and Kenya's Kemboi Kiprop.
